**Unblocked — #6419 is closed, re-measured on the merged ref, and the re-measurement corrects this card.**

Triage's `Blocked-by: #6419` resolves: #6419 closed `completed`. Triage's unlock note asked for two things before this moves — *"on #6419 close, re-measure on the merged ref, then the executing seat answers the card's real design choice"*. Both are below.

## Re-measured on `main`

The defect is still there; #6419's merge did not remove it, exactly as this card predicted. `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` on `main` right now:

```
:720   const activeView = viewsPropResolved?.find(v => v.id === currentActiveViewId) || viewsPropResolved?.[0];
:762   useEffect(() => {                      <- the non-grid fetch effect
:914-918   }, [
             schema.objectName, dataSource, currentViewType, refreshKey,
             currentNamedViewConfig, activeView, renderListView,
             objectSchemaReady, objectSchema,
           ]);
```

`objectSchemaReady` / `objectSchema` are #6419's gate arriving in the array, which is the 4→3 shift this card recorded in advance. `activeView` is untouched at `:916`.

## ⚠️ The card is wrong about which fields the effect reads, and the correction changes the fix

This card states: *"The effect only ever reads `activeView?.filter` and `activeView?.type` (the latter via `currentViewType`, which is already its own dependency)."*

Measured inside the effect body on `main`, `activeView` is read at exactly two sites, and the second is **not** `type`:

```
:825   currentNamedViewConfig?.filter || activeView?.filter || schema.table?.filter || schema.table?.defaultFilters
:860   currentNamedViewConfig?.sort   || activeView?.sort   || schema.table?.sort   || (schema.table?.defaultSort ? [schema.table.defaultSort] : undefined)
```

So it is **`filter` and `sort`**. A fix built on the card's sentence — depend on `activeView?.id` plus filter identity — would silently drop the sort dependency, and a host that changes only a view's `sort` would stop re-fetching. That is a worse defect than the churn being fixed, and it would pass any test written from the card's own text. Note also that both reads sit *behind* `currentNamedViewConfig`, so `activeView`'s value only reaches the query when the named-view config does not supply that key.

## The design choice, answered by this seat

Triage delegated it and marked its own suggestion as *"a suggestion, not a ruling"*. Ruling for dispatch:

- **Taken — depend on the identity of what the effect actually reads** (`filter` and `sort`, per the correction above), not on the `activeView` object. Mechanism is the implementer's, with one constraint: it must survive a filter or sort value that does not round-trip through naive stringification.
- **Rejected — "ask hosts for a stable array."** That is a demand on every caller of a published component, i.e. a contract change dressed as a bug fix, and it leaves the defect in place for every host that does not comply.

This direction is convergence rather than invention: the same file already derives a stable string key from the fields it cares about at `:1639` — `` `${schema.objectName}-${activeNamedView || activeView?.id || 'default'}-${currentViewType}-${refreshKey}` `` — so the pattern is in-file precedent, not a new idea introduced by this card.

Scope stays this one effect. `activeView` also sits in three other dependency arrays (`:727`, `:1108`, `:1380`, `:1474`); they are out of scope here and are not to be swept in as riders.

Returned to `pm:queue` and dispatched this round.

## Notes for the PM, beyond the JSON

**The dispatch order was right to make me re-measure, and one of its numbers changed.** The card's 4 vs 1 is what I observe on the merge base; the "3 post-#6419" is a property of the card's timer harness, not of the code. Stated as an invariant instead of a count: **before the fix each parent re-render costs exactly one extra `find`, after it zero.**

**The card's field list was wrong in the way the PM said, and I confirmed it independently** — `activeView` is read at exactly two sites inside the effect and the second is `sort`. `re-fetches when only the view's SORT changes` is a committed control, so a future fix cannot quietly drop it.

**Line numbers**: the merge base matches the PM's dispatch-time reading exactly (`:720` derivation, `:825` filter read, `:860` sort read, `:914-918` dep array, `:1639` display key). Nothing had moved.

**One thing I chose not to file.** `currentNamedViewConfig` is also in this effect's dependency array and is a `useMemo` over `schema.listViews`, so a host that inlines its `schema` object could churn this effect through that door instead. It is out of this card's stated scope (the ruling is about `activeView`), and I did not measure it — so I recorded it in the PR's Scope section rather than filing a card on an unmeasured suspicion. If you want it as a finding, it needs its own measurement first.

**Also not filed**: the four other `activeView` dependency arrays (`:727`, `:1108`, `:1380`, `:1474`) named as out of scope. They are untouched and unmeasured; same reasoning.

**Post-merge verification — PR #6582 merged 2026-08-26T15:01Z. Measured on `main`, all four axes clean.**

**The fix.** `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` (2006 lines): the non-grid fetch effect's dependency array at `:955` carries `activeViewQueryInputs`, produced by `useStableIdentity` at `:755`. `packages/plugin-view/src/stableIdentity.ts` is present at 142 lines.

**⛔ Constraint 1 — precedence unflattened.** Both reads still sit behind `currentNamedViewConfig` in the same `||` chains:

```
:864   currentNamedViewConfig?.filter || activeViewQueryInputs?.filter
:899   currentNamedViewConfig?.sort   || activeViewQueryInputs?.sort
```

**⛔ Constraint 2 — the four other dependency arrays untouched.** All present, all still carrying a bare `activeView`, none swept in as riders:

```
 :766   }, [currentNamedViewConfig, activeView, schema.defaultViewType]);
:1147   }, [hasMultiView, viewsPropResolved, activeView, schema.objectName, …]);
:1419   }, [schema.objectName, schema.table?.columns, schema.table?.fields, currentNamedViewConfig, activeView]);
:1513   }, [schema, operations, currentNamedViewConfig, activeView]);
```

**Published surface unchanged.** `packages/plugin-view/src/index.tsx` has **14** export lines (the control fires, so the file was genuinely read) and **0** occurrences of `stableIdentity` / `StableIdentity`. The new module stays internal, which is what makes the patch-level changeset right.

## ⚠️ Instrument correction — the first pass reported constraint 2 as `count = 0`

That read as a regression: four dependency arrays that were present on the branch, apparently gone from `main`. They were never gone. The shell pattern `^\s*\}, \[.*activeView[,\]]` contains a bracket expression `[,\]]`, and inside a POSIX bracket expression a backslash is **not** an escape — it parses as "one of `,` or `\`", followed by a literal `]` outside the bracket. So the pattern demanded `activeView` be followed by a backslash-then-bracket sequence that occurs nowhere, and returned an empty set that looked exactly like a finding.

Re-run with a control first — `activeView` appears **72** times in the file, so the target is plainly there — all four arrays come back at the line numbers above.

This is the third instrument fault caught during verification in this session, after a shell-quoting error that made a `heavyDomTests` check read an empty list, and a `grep … | sed … || echo` whose fallback bound to `sed` and so never fired on empty input. **Every one of the three was caught by a positive control, and none by suspicion** — which is the argument for running the control first rather than only when a result looks odd. A zero that matches your expectations is the one you never re-check.

Nothing outstanding on this card.
